declaration_findings.finding: The all-position identity is derived from exhaustive actual B/old positions. In the B branch actual new-label collapse and collapse_B both give the actual root position of j; in the retained branch old-label collapse and collapse_old recover the same parent label. No supplied root-word correspondence appears.

The sole excluded position is actual B. old_collapse_of_ne_B reconstructs every other position, and the complete old-index theorem then gives the physical retained old label, including A. This is exactly the input needed to evaluate the remaining vertex of either exceptional triple.

The rational entry is the actual softFarSign at boundaryIndex g k, with the source negative determinant orientation, cast through Int. It is not an arbitrary far array or caller-chosen sign correspondence. Its value at the distinguished occurrence may be zero and is intentionally not constrained.

The hypothesis k != softRootPosition is transported to the physical label != j by boundaryIndex injectivity and softRootPosition_index. Admissibility supplies nonzero softFarSign, then the exhaustive SignType sign_square lemma supplies square one. This condition is derived in the final theorem, never supplied as a geometric premise.

The actual array reads chi in upper,middle,lower order. Strict IncreasingBoundaryTriple inequalities and boundaryIndex injectivity give all three required pairwise distinctness conditions. Parent G1 then gives nonzero chi, and the same exact SignType cast calculation yields square one on every core triple.

The two root-relative indices are explicitly softRootPosition(j-1)g and softRootPosition(j+1)g. Evaluation gives the physical predecessor and successor labels and the frozen exact attachmentMinus/Plus signs. This covers cyclic wrap of j. It does not separately declare an equality of these Fin positions with a future positional cyclic-predecessor/successor API.

The literal A and B indices are rewritten to actual softOldIndex j j and softNewIndex j. Injectivity of boundaryIndex converts physical membership in the reversed triple support back to the exact three position equalities defining tripleContainsBoth. Thus a plain increasing triple cannot accidentally include the two physical attachment occurrences.

For middle=A and upper=B, strictness makes lower != B. The old-collapse identity identifies its actual core vertex. Since geometricBoundaryArray reverses the increasing triple, its chi is (B,A,X), exactly softFarSign_exceptional.1. The result reads t at the collapsed lower endpoint; no sign flip or wrong order is introduced.

For lower=A and middle=B, strictness makes upper != B. The reversed geometric chi is (Y,B,A), exactly the cyclic counterpart softFarSign_exceptional.2. It reads t at the collapsed upper endpoint. Both exceptional identities are exact for every positive epsilon; they do not use a guessed continuity sign for the vanishing triple.

The pointwise bridge explicitly exposes its physical pullback premise. It derives three distinct physical labels and avoidance from the actual increasing boundary triple, applies that premise, then rewrites all three collapse indices and casts the sign equality. collapseTriple has precisely these three collapsed positions with strictness proved in the frozen array dependency. The final aggregate derives this bridge premise from the source hypotheses.

The existential positive radius is obtained once from soft_far_sign_family before the universal root g. On that interval child G1 and every root-independent nonexceptional physical pullback are available. For each root, function extensionality and the exhaustive consecutive A/B triple classification split the array into upper exception, lower exception, and plain cases. Each branch uses the actual geometry bridge. The core and exceptional square conditions are simultaneously derived from parent G1 and admissibility. No child Generic/G1 at epsilon=0, supplied array correspondence, arbitrary sign-square premise, or already-proved duplication output occurs.

boundary_and_exhaustion_checks: The source has n=M+1 with M>=2. The aggregate includes n=3 and never invokes a two-gon amplitude. It uses G1, a sufficient weaker geometric input than source Generic for this bounded sign-array conclusion.

Incoming root g=j-1 has s=0; only the lower exceptional case can occur. Return root g=j has s=n-1; only the upper exceptional case can occur. In both cases tripleLift and actual geometric evaluation include all increasing triples. For interior s, the two exceptional cases are disjoint and all other triples have a strict collapsed triple.

The physical old/new root correspondence is derived by frozen SoftRootBoundary for arbitrary j,g, including j=0 and numerical cyclic wrap. Its nonsoft theorem proves every actual nonsoft child root has a unique such parent root; the new aggregate uses all parent roots through this exact child-root map. No freely supplied root mapping is assumed.

Exceptional third arguments never equal s: the upper exception collapses a position strictly before A, and the lower exception collapses a position strictly after B. Therefore the source allows t only away from A, even though Lean represents t as a total function with a possibly zero value at A.

The proof uses a finite common continuity neighborhood rather than the displayed explicit delta/K estimate. This establishes the same positive-tail sign constancy and is uniform across all roots. The stronger source family tail can later be imposed by taking the minimum with its own positive radius; the present statement does not claim return-edge/crossing-family data.
All listed boundary checks are direct source/definition/proof analysis. No new Lean consumers or kernel executions were run by this reviewer.
